chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:
The Aqeeqa is obligatory when a child is born to a man, so if he wishes to name him on that day, let him do so.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: Al-Abd al-Salih: A title for Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), the 7th Imam.
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: The ritual sacrifice of an animal performed upon the birth of a child.
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: Obligatory: A legal ruling indicating a mandatory act in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Aqeeqa in Shia Islam and when should it be performed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Aqeeqa as an obligatory act (wajib) for a father upon the birth of a child, linking the ritual sacrifice directly to the naming ceremony. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this ruling through prominent Shia authorities, emphasizing its status as a confirmed Sunnah with legal weight. Practically, it underscores the importance of early gratitude to Allah and the public declaration of the child's identity within the family structure.
